TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.FitPortraitToRi: When auto-applying the default ring, scale the portrait so its largest side fits within the ring's inner boundary.

TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.DefaultMaskHint: Optional mask image applied to token content instead of the auto-generated ring mask. Use a square image where opaque areas are visible. Leave empty to auto-detect the mask from the ring.

TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.AvatarLocations: Default server folders where exported avatar/portrait images are saved.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.AvatarNameHint: Filename templates for saved avatars. Use {{name}} for actor name, {{id}} for actor ID, {{tokenId}} for placed token ID.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.ApplyDefaultBac: Automatically add the default background image as the bottom layer when opening a new token in the editor.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.BackgroundHint: Default background texture or image placed beneath all layers when a new editor session opens.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.ApplyDefaultCol: Automatically add a solid colour layer at the bottom of the stack when opening a new token in the editor. Sits beneath the background image if both are enabled.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.AdvancedHint: Advanced settings for troubleshooting and integration.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.ExportSizeHint: Resolution of the exported token image. Larger sizes produce sharper tokens but use more storage.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.ExportFormatHin: File format for saved token images. WebP produces smaller files; use PNG for maximum compatibility.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.ProxyUrlHint: Prepended to external http(s) image URLs to avoid CORS errors. Leave empty to disable. The source URL is appended directly after this value.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.RayMaskEdgeMode: Default edge-pixel pick for auto-generated frame ray masks. Highest Alpha matches Tokenizer 1 and gives cleaner edges on anti-aliased frames; First Opaque stops at the first solid pixel. Can be overridden per frame in the Masks panel.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.RayMaskSampleSi: Default for auto-generated frame ray masks: cast every Nth ray when tracing the frame's inner window. Higher values give a coarser, smoother outline (Tokenizer 1 used 5); 1 is densest. Can be overridden per frame in the Masks panel.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.DisableLayerPer: When enabled, intermediate tool results are kept in memory instead of being uploaded to the server, and the layer stack is not saved to actor data. The editor always starts fresh when reopened. Reduces disk usage in cache and paste folders.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.SaveDynamicText: Save Regular Texture with Dynamic Token
When saving a dynamic ring token, also write the image path to the regular texture field (prototypeToken.texture.src). Disabled by default.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.BakeDynamicRing: Save Dynamic Ring into Regular Texture

When the regular texture is saved with a dynamic ring token, it gets the ring drawn in, so the token still has its ring if the dynamic ring is turned off. It is saved as a second image next to the token, named with -ring. Enabled by default.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.DisableTokenFra: When the Token Frames (jColson) module is installed, its frames are shown as an additional tab in the Frame Browser. Enable this to hide that tab without uninstalling the module.
The Token Frames module is not installed - nothing to hide.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.UseDynamicRingD: Use Foundry Dynamic Ring by default
When enabled, new editor sessions use Foundry's native dynamic ring system instead of baking the ring into the token image. The ring appears as a non-exportable preview layer during editing.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.DefaultOversize: Enable the oversized ring automatically on first open so the token spills into surrounding spaces.

How much larger than its square an oversized token is made when the editor first opens it. With ring fill, a Dynamic Ring token grows whole so its ring fills the square; tokens with frames are made 1.3×.
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.RingStyleDefaul: The style the Ring Generator starts on, to match your table's token art (cartoon, ink, flat or pixel). Each frame can still be made in another style.
TOKENIZER-2.RingToolsFrameBrowserHint: Pick a frame or ring image to add as a layer.

TOKENIZER-2.RingToolsConditionRingsHint: Edit the rings shown on map tokens for conditions, and which condition shows which ring.
TOKENIZER-2.RingToolsOrnamentRulesHint: Choose which ornaments actors get on the map (opens the settings on the Ornaments tab).
TOKENIZER-2.RingToolsNumberBadgesHint: Number copies of a creature on the map, and choose where badges sit (opens the settings on the Number Badges tab).
TOKENIZER-2.RingToolsBadgeDesignsHint: Make and change the number badge designs.
TOKENIZER-2.OversizedHintSmall: Draws the token 1.3× the size of its square. The frame or ring keeps its size, with a little room past it for the art.
TOKENIZER-2.OversizedHintRingFill: Draws the whole token, ring and art, 1.3× larger, so Foundry's ring fills the square instead of sitting inside it. Foundry's Grid fit mode (Dynamic Token Rings Fit Modes in Core settings) does this for every token without scaling them.
TOKENIZER-2.OversizedHintLarge: Draws the token twice the size of its square, so parts of it can spill over the squares around it.
TOKENIZER-2.FrameOverflowWarning: This frame reaches past the token's edge, so its outer parts are cut off. Turn on Oversized (2×) to show all of it.

TOKENIZER-2.Tour.Title: Getting Started with Tokenizer 2
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.Description: A quick guided tour of the token image editor.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.EditorMustBeOpen: Open the Tokenizer 2 editor first, then start the tour.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.WelcomeContent: This is your canvas - where you compose a token from multiple layers. The editor has three columns: adjustments on the left, the canvas in the centre, and layers on the right.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.ZoomContent: Use these buttons to zoom in, out, or reset the view. You can also scroll the mouse wheel to zoom, and drag with the middle mouse button or hold Space to pan.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.UndoRedoContent: Made a mistake? Undo and redo your changes here. Undo steps back through your last 20 changes whichever tool made them. Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+Z to undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z to redo.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.AnimationContent: Give any layer an animation preset (rotate, breathe, pulse, shimmer) from its Adjustments panel, or drop in a .webm / .mp4. When anything is animated a play button appears here for live preview, and saving writes a looping .webm.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.SaveContent: When you're done, click Save to write the token image back to the actor. You can also Download a copy, use Quick Token presets, or open Settings.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.ModeToggleContent: Switch between Token and Avatar editing modes. Token mode produces a circular token image with frames and rings. Avatar mode lets you edit the actor's portrait at any aspect ratio. Each mode keeps its own layer stack. The arrows button copies what you are looking at into the other mode, so you can update token and portrait together.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.LayerPanelContent: The right panel is where you manage your layer stack, frames, and masks. Layers are composited from bottom to top - just like image editors you may already know.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.LayerListContent: Click a layer to select it. Drag layers to reorder them. Each layer has visibility and lock toggles on the right. Double-click a layer name to rename it. Right click on a layer for more options.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.AddLayersContent: Click the + button to add new layers: images from your files, the actor's avatar or existing token, text overlays, mask images, or a painted mask you draw by hand.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.FrameRingContent: Browse the built-in frame library, design your own in the Frame Browser's Ring Generator tab, or add a shape ring to give your token a border. Frames automatically mask the layers below them.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.MasksTabContent: The Masks tab gives you a global view of every mask across all layers. You can add, remove, and configure masks for any layer without having to select it first. Masks control which parts of a layer are visible - use alpha, ring, or frame-based masks to shape your token.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.ToolsContent: The toolbar offers several editing tools: Palette (move/adjust), Transform, Magic Lasso, Freehand Lasso, Liquify, Erase/Restore, Clone/Heal, and Layer Effects. Click a tool to activate it.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.LeftPanelContent: The left panel shows contextual controls for the active tool and selected layer - brightness, contrast, opacity, tint, blend mode, and more. It updates automatically as you switch tools.
TOKENIZER-2.Tour.MinimapContent: The minimap shows your full token composition. Drag the viewport rectangle to quickly pan around when zoomed in. That's the end of the tour - happy tokenizing!
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.Enabled: Give tokens ornaments from their actors
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.EnabledHint: Auto-Tokenize, batch tokenizing and the editor (when it starts a new token) lay an ornament over the frame, chosen by the rules below: a crown for a boss, laurels for an elite, a shield for an ally, pips for a tier. Ornaments use the Ring Generator's default style. A token that is not oversized gets its ornament set lower, over the ring, so it fits.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.NumberBadges: Number copies of the same creature on the map
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.NumberBadgesHint: When two or more tokens of the same unlinked actor are on a scene, each gets a number badge (1, 2, 3...) on its frame, so players can tell them apart. Numbers stay with their tokens; a removed token's number is given to the next copy. A GM must be connected to give out numbers.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.TokenConditionsHin: Draws a ring effect around each token for its current conditions (blinded, frightened, grappled, on fire and so on), in the Ring Generator's style, alongside Foundry's status icons. It follows the token's statuses as they change and is not saved into the token image. A condition's image is made the first time a token needs it, by a connected GM, so it can take a few seconds to appear the first time.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.TokenConditionsMax: A token with more conditions shows the first ones in the order its statuses list them. Dead is always shown on its own.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.PrepareConditionsH: {made} of {total} condition images are made in the current ring style. Making them all now (under a minute) means conditions appear at once the first time.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.PrepareConditionsS: Making the condition images for tokens. This takes under a minute.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.RulesHint: Checked from the top: the first rule that matches picks the ornament, and an actor matching none gets no ornament. "No ornament" stops the check, so put it first to leave, say, player characters alone. Tier pips show the actor's tier, 1 to 5.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.FieldPathHint: The actor data to read, as a path (such as system.details.type.value)
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.DesignsHint: Where each kind of ornament sits on the ring and how, and optionally your own picture in place of the built-in crest (not for tier pips). Depth sets it lower into the ring; below zero raises it. On a token that is not oversized, it is set at least low enough to fit.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.DepthHint: How far into the ring the ornament is set; below zero raises it.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.MirrorHint: Adds its mirror image on the other side of the ring, for pairs such as wings.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.RepeatArcHint: With Repeat above 1: 360 spaces the copies evenly all round the ring; less spreads them across that many degrees, centred on the position.
TOKENIZER-2.ORNAMENTS.DesignImagePlaceho: Leave empty for the built-in crest
TOKENIZER-2.RING_GEN.EffectAddHint: Draw a frame effect (damage, blood, frost, flames, slime, a power failure) or a condition into the ring.
TOKENIZER-2.RING_GEN.EffectLimit: A ring can carry up to 8 effects.

TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.GMOnly: Only a Gamemaster can export or import Tokenizer 2 settings.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.TabHint: Save your Tokenizer 2 settings to use in other worlds, or as a file to keep or share. You can save everything, or just your condition rings and mappings, ring themes, ornament rules or custom frames.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.Following: This world follows the backup "{name}" (version {version}): you will be offered newer versions when they are saved.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.ExportHint: Choose what to include, then save it to module storage (for other worlds on this server) or download it as a file.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.Name: Name
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.NextVersion: Saves "{name}" as version {version}. Worlds that follow it are offered the update.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.NameTaken: There is already a backup called "{name}": saving makes its version {version}.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.NoneStored: No backups saved in module storage yet.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.Merge: Add to your existing themes, frames and condition rings (rather than replacing them)
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.Follow: Offer me newer versions of this backup
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.NoChanges: Nothing would change: your settings already match.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.OfferIntro: Tokenizer 2 settings backups were found in module storage. Would you like to import one into this world?
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.UpdateIntro: A newer version of the settings backup "{name}" is available: version {version} (this world has version {current}), saved from {world} on {date}.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.NotABackup: That file is not a Tokenizer 2 settings backup.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.NothingChosen: Choose at least one thing to include.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.Skipped: {count} world settings were skipped: only a Gamemaster can change them.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.Unfollowed: This world no longer follows that backup.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.Failed: The settings backup failed. See the console for details.
TOKENIZER-2.BACKUP.ReloadPrompt: Some settings only take effect after a reload. Reload Foundry now?
TOKENIZER-2.BADGES.DefaultHint: Badges use this design unless a rule below picks another. Click a design to choose it.
TOKENIZER-2.BADGES.RulesEnabledHint: Off by default: every badge uses the default design. Turn on to let the rules below pick a design for each kind of creature.
TOKENIZER-2.BADGES.RulesHint: Checked from the top for the game system in use; the first rule that matches picks the badge's design. For example, undead get bone badges and fiends infernal ones.
TOKENIZER-2.BADGES.ApplyHint: Saving redraws the badges on the current scene in their new look. Their numbers stay the same.
TOKENIZER-2.BADGES.PlacementHint: Every badge sits here on its token's frame, whatever its design. Changing it moves the badges on the map without redrawing them.
TOKENIZER-2.BADGE_EDITOR.Title: Badge Designs
TOKENIZER-2.BADGE_EDITOR.GMOnly: Only a Gamemaster can edit badge designs.
TOKENIZER-2.BADGE_EDITOR.PreviewHint: Badges 1, 7 and 12 on sample tokens, placed as the map places them. A prefix from the creature's initial shows as G, for a goblin.
TOKENIZER-2.BADGE_EDITOR.ReadOnly: Built-in designs cannot be changed. Duplicate one to make your own.
TOKENIZER-2.BADGE_EDITOR.Name: Name
TOKENIZER-2.BADGE_EDITOR.UnsavedClose: Close without saving your changes to the badge designs?
TOKENIZER-2.SETTINGS_APP.RingStyleOption: What the style draws with: ink and paper colours, the spacing of hatching, strokes or dots, the pixel art's pixel size and how far watercolour bleeds. The Ring Generator starts on these, and number badges, ornaments and conditions on tokens are drawn with them.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.Title: Dynamic Rings
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.SettingsHint: Turn Ring Generator designs into Foundry dynamic token rings. Rings you add to Foundry's list can be chosen in Core settings under Dynamic Token Ring, or made the world's ring from the manager.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.GMOnly: Only a GM can manage dynamic rings.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.NotFound: That dynamic ring no longer exists.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.ReloadNeeded: Foundry reads its dynamic rings when the world loads. Reload to bring in your changes.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.ListHint: Tick a ring to add it to Foundry's list of dynamic rings.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.InFoundryList: In Foundry's list of dynamic rings
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.Empty: No dynamic rings yet. Press New to design one in the Ring Generator, or From picture to use a ring picture.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.DeleteConfirm: Delete the dynamic ring "{label}"? If it is the world's ring, the world goes back to Foundry's steel ring.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.Name: Name
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.StatusInList: In Foundry's list of dynamic rings.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.StatusWorldRin: In Foundry's list, and the ring this world uses.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.StatusOutdated: Foundry still has an older version of this ring: Redraw to update it.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.Activated: "{label}" is now the world's dynamic ring.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.RegenerateHint: Draw the ring's image for Foundry again, for example after its files were deleted.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.ColourModeHint: The ring looks exactly as designed. Token ring colours, and the pulse and gradient effects, change nothing.
Foundry colours part of the ring with each token's ring colour, and the pulse and gradient effects work. Choose below what it colours. Tokens with no ring colour show the default colour.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.BackgroundMode: Mid grey (takes the token's background colour exactly)
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.Shrunk: This design reaches far past its band, so it is drawn a little smaller than Foundry's rings to fit the token.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.EditHint: The ring's name, colours, background, picture and design are changed in the Ring Generator, and saved there with Update Dynamic Ring.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.NoneSelected: Pick a ring on the left, or make a new one.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.PreviewHint: Try a token's colours here; they are not saved. The swatches are Foundry's disposition colours.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.NewHint: Design a ring in the Ring Generator; its Dynamic Ring button makes it a dynamic ring.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.ImportConflict: This world already has the dynamic ring "{label}". Replace it, or add the imported one as a copy?
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.SheetsRemade: Tokenizer redrew {count} dynamic ring image(s) for Foundry.
TOKENIZER-2.RING_GEN.DynamicRingHint: Turn this design into one of Foundry's dynamic token rings: a ring Foundry draws around every token on the map, which can take each token's colour. The ring is saved to the world and this window carries on editing it, with its name, colouring and background under In Foundry.
TOKENIZER-2.RING_GEN.UpdateDynamicRingHi: Save this dynamic ring: its design and everything under In Foundry. If the ring is in Foundry's list, its image for Foundry is drawn again.
TOKENIZER-2.RING_GEN.OpenDynamicRingsHin: Open the Dynamic Rings window on this ring: the world's rings, which of them Foundry offers, and which one the world uses.
TOKENIZER-2.RING_GEN.AddFrameHint: Draw the ring at full size and add it to the token as a frame layer. It is kept in your Custom frames too.
TOKENIZER-2.RING_GEN.ResetHint: Back to the theme as you picked it, or the frame or dynamic ring as it was saved.
TOKENIZER-2.RING_GEN.DynamicRingExportHi: Download this design as a dynamic ring file. A GM can import it in the Dynamic Rings manager.
TOKENIZER-2.DynamicRingFullColourHint: This ring is drawn in full colour, so a ring colour changes nothing.
TOKENIZER-2.RingToolsDynamicRingsHint: Turn Ring Generator designs into Foundry dynamic token rings and choose the world's ring.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.FromPictureHin: Make a dynamic ring from a ring picture you already have: pick it in the Frame Browser.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.PictureNotFoun: Tokenizer could not find a ring in that picture. Set where the ring starts and ends by hand.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.PictureHint: This ring is drawn from a picture. Tokenizer measured where its ring starts and ends; adjust them if the preview does not line up. They are measured from the centre, as a share of the picture's half-width.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.RemeasureHint: Find where the picture's ring starts and ends again, undoing your changes to them.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.TintAreaHint.b: The ring between the two edges below is drawn in grey, and Foundry colours it.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.TintAreaHint.c: Only the parts of the ring in the colours you pick (such as its lights or gems) take the token's ring colour; everything else keeps its own colours. The edges below limit where on the ring they are picked.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.Eyedropper: Pick colours by clicking the ring in the preview
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.PickingHint: Click the ring in the preview to pick its colours; click the eyedropper again when you are done.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.Highlight: Show the tinted parts in magenta
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.ActivateNeedsL: Add the ring to Foundry's list first.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.ActivateHint: Make this the ring every token in the world uses. Foundry changes rings when the world reloads.
TOKENIZER-2.DYNAMIC_RINGS.PictureBackgro: The picture fills the disc behind the token. A token's background tint colour is blended over it, keeping its light and dark detail; a mid-grey texture takes the colour most faithfully.
TOKENIZER-2.Nudge.CoatOfArmsContent: Did you know Tokenizer 2 has a Coat of Arms generator plugin? Install it the usual way, and find out more at {link}.
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.Title: Tokenizer 2
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.MenuHint: Things players have sent for your approval, such as a coat of arms.
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.GMOnly: Only a GM can review player requests.
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.Arrived: {player} sent {label} for your approval. Review it from its chat card.
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.WaitingAtLogin: {count} player request(s) are waiting for your approval. Review them from their chat cards, or in Tokenizer 2's Player Requests settings.
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.Error.unknown-ty: This kind of request is not known here; the module that sends it may be missing or disabled.
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.Error.not-owner: Only an owner of this character can send a request for it.
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.Error.invalid: The request could not be read.
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.Error.old-versio: The request was made by a different version of Tokenizer 2; ask the player to send it again.
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.Error.gone: That request is no longer waiting.
TOKENIZER-2.GM_REQUESTS.Error.apply-fail: The request could not be applied: {error}
